details.publicNotes:
At first glance, this plant resembles a massive fern, with spiky leaves sprouting along thin, rigid branches. A big, reddish-brown fruit grows at the center of the plant, almost like a heart. The fruit digests ambient void energy as well as void energy extracted from other rich sources. While a blood fern's favored prey are undead creatures, the ferns lack the intelligence to distinguish between living and dead, so they attack all that cross their paths indiscriminately. The only surefire way to pacify a blood fern is to feed it enough void energy to calm it into a temporary stupor.

Blood ferns spontaneously arise in the aftermath of major outbursts of void energy. These events tend to corrupt the land and kill most living creatures. Sometimes, however, plants can withstand these energies and absorb them. In some cases, this energy is so overwhelming that it changes the physiology of the plant itself, slowly turning it into a blood fern in the span of a couple of weeks.

Some alchemical manuals posit that the nectar from a blood fern's fruit could be brewed into a concoction that would allow a living creature to walk the line between life and death, but experiments on this subject have all too often ended in tragedy. Vampires use the nectar in rituals to create sanguine roses, in place of the typical black onyx.

Blood Fern Hollows

Druids and other stewards of nature often hold conflicting opinions regarding blood ferns. On one hand, blood ferns are not natural creations, and in an area where void energy isn't prevalent, the ferns can upset the region's delicate ecosystem. On the other hand, given time, blood ferns can cleanse a forest tainted with void energy, filtering the energy from their surroundings like a normal plant would purify an atmosphere of toxic gases. This is why some druids intentionally cultivate stands of blood ferns, hiding the plants in tucked-away hollows until they are required. When the forest faces invasion, the druids might herd the intruders into these hollows or activate and march the ferns directly toward the threat.

description.value: The blood fern can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.XMcnh4cSI32tljXa]{Hide} in natural forest or grassland environments even if it doesn't have cover.

Trigger A creature bites into the blood fern (such as by making a successful jaws Strike)

Effect The poisonous fruit at the center of the blood fern explodes in a burst of toxic nectar. All creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] take @Damage[3d6[poison],3d6[void]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:32|basic] save). The blood fern can't use Toxic Burst again until the fruit regrows, a process that takes about 24 hours.
When a blood fern is destroyed while its fruit is still intact, the fruit automatically explodes. This has the effects of Toxic Burst.

The strong roots of the blood fern dig in search of fresh blood. At the end of the blood fern's turn, all creatures @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} by the blood fern take @Damage[3d6[void]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:29|basic] save). Undead grabbed by the blood fern instead take @Damage[3d6[force]] damage, as the plant leeches void energy from their bodies. The blood fern can maintain a grapple with up to four creatures with its roots.

The blood fern uproots itself and pounces atop its prey, crushing them beneath its strong roots. The fern drops all grappled creatures, then Leaps 10 feet into an area that contains at least one creature. Each creature in the area where the blood fern lands takes @Damage[4d6[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:29|basic] save). The blood fern then immediately attempts Athletics checks to grapple up to four creatures that failed the Reflex save; these attempts neither apply nor count toward the blood fern's multiple attack penalty. All creatures in the area are then moved in the closest unoccupied square adjacent to the blood fern; this is forced movement.
